title: Audit Log
markdown:
The audit log is a persistent, searchable, append-only record of what the system did — distinct from episodic memory (which biases future LLM behavior). Every event flows through `audit/logger.log_event`, a synchronous SQLite writer (WAL + 5s busy_timeout) that appends one row to the `audit_log` table in `episodic_memory.db`.

### Event types
Rows are tagged by `event_type`, including `chat_turn`, `specialist_consult`, `tool_invocation`, `scheduled_action`, `alert`, `integration_inbound` (Slack / Discord / email / Telegram / Google Chat), plus `knowledge_retrieval`, `cache_event`, `memory_snapshot`, `committee_review`, `peer_memory`, `narration_policy_violation`, and the external-signal/monitor events.

`narration_policy_violation` is a log-only guardrail: after a turn's response text is finalized, a regex claim-detector (`orchestrator.narration_integrity`) checks whether the text narrates a specialist consult (e.g. "after checking with our CFO...") while no specialist was actually dispatched that turn. A match is logged with the matched phrase and the full response text — it never blocks, retries, or modifies the response the user receives. It exists to gather real data on false-positive rates (ordinary advice-giving phrasing can also match) before any runtime enforcement is considered. Known gaps: it's turn-level rather than per-specialist (a real consult to any specialist suppresses detection of a fabricated claim naming a different one); on committee turns it checks the discarded internal draft, not the revision actually delivered to the user (the row's `details.phase` is `"committee_draft"` vs `"final"` so these are distinguishable — a `committee_draft` row can be a false positive or false negative relative to what shipped); and cross-iteration text accumulation (needed to catch preamble fabrication before a forced consult) can also flag preamble before an unrelated skill/MCP tool call.

### Session & turn context
Each row carries `session_id`, `turn_id`, `actor`, `summary`, `details_json`, `full_json`, and `department`. A `turn_id` (`f"t-{uuid12}"`) is set per Executive turn and propagated automatically via ContextVars to retriever / specialist / tool / cache emits, grouping one user-assistant exchange. `summary` is the searchable column (LIKE, ~300 char cap); `details_json` is structured and not searched.

### Views
- `GET /audit` — filterable list with a "Group by session" toggle and session pills.
- `GET /audit/session/{id}` — full ordered timeline plus a server-derived node/edge graph rendered as a three-pane React Flow chart.

### Invariant
Audit writes never break a chat turn: all writes swallow exceptions and log a warning, and instrumentation observes only — it never touches request building or the cached prompt blocks. Audit is append-only: no UPDATE or DELETE paths exist in product code.
